governance.determination: REJECTED PROBE (path B is a no-op for the downstate tail; the measured synchronised-reserve requirement does not bind). Keeper stays nyiso-27 cc-offer (keepers.json[NYISO] unchanged).
governance.note: Re-solve of the nyiso-27 cc-offer keeper config (byte-identical keeper flags: --gas-monthly-actuals --gas-hub-basis-overlay --gas-hub-basis-daily --priced-interchange --energy-reserve-coopt --nyiso-local-selfsupply --nyiso-firm-imports --nyiso-import-reconciliation) plus the path-B route of the NYISO-only, default-OFF --nyiso-synchronised-reserve lever WITH the P2 commitment screen ON (--commitment). Path B (docs/handoffs/nyiso-downstate-reserve-incidence-2026-06.md, 'Path B') replaces path A's online-gated proxy row with COMMITMENT as the online indicator: (1) the NYC spinning family rides the ORDINARY class-1 (quick-start) headroom row (Sum P + R <= Sum cap), and apply_commitment_with_coal_pin zeroes the availability of decommitted units so that, restricted to the committed set, the row equals Sum_online(pmax - P) -- the physically-correct synchronised headroom, MILP-free; (2) a new reserve-adequacy commit (model.commitment.reserve_adequacy_commit, wired in runner P2) force-commits the cheapest-startup NYC quick-start units until committed capacity covers the MEASURED NYC spinning requirement = NYISO_SPIN_FRACTION x NYC 10-min total = 0.5 x 500 = 250 MW (the published 1/2-largest-contingency rule; a market-design constant, NOT fitted). PURPOSE: test whether commitment-gated synchronised headroom binds the NYC reserve family endogenously and fires the >$300 RCPF tail.
governance.validation_note: No scored OUTPUT is pinned and NO price adder is added -- the >$300 tail in this run is whatever the binding reserve family endogenously produces (here: it does NOT fire, see below). The single new quantity is a measured INPUT: the spinning fraction 0.5 (NYISO Ancillary Services / T&D Operations Manual: 10-min spinning = 1/2 largest contingency) applied to the already-grounded NYC 10-min total, and the committed-headroom target was set TO that measured 250 MW requirement (nyiso_spin_headroom_frac=1.0), NOT raised to whatever value would manufacture the missing tail hours (forbidden, rule #12). The gas total and LMP remain unpinned; no unit pinned to CEMS; no haircut/adder/sigmoid tuned to a residual; the td_loss / gas-basis floor is untouched.

_probe_outcome: REJECTED PROBE -- path B is a TRUE NO-OP for the downstate scarcity tail AND the CT_PEAKER energy: every scored metric reproduces the nyiso-27 keeper essentially exactly (C1 CT_PEAKER 2023 -1.30, 2024 -1.51 TWh; C1 CC_REGULAR 2023 +1.70, 2024 +2.09; C3c >$300 1/0/8 vs actual 10/12/42; C3a 2024 -9.7%; C3b 2024 NRMSE 0.243; C2 gas 2025 -3.8%; C5a 2024 -9.1%). P1 and P2 clear at IDENTICAL prices and the NYC quick-start fleet generates the identical 2.231 TWh in P1 and P2, so the commitment screen + reserve-adequacy commit changed nothing the reserve clearing sees. ROOT CAUSE (the decisive empirical finding, distinct from path A's): the physically-correct synchronised headroom Sum_online(pmax - P) over the COMMITTED NYC quick-start fleet is ABUNDANT relative to the measured requirement, even in the tightest hours. In the top-50 NYC-price hours of 2025 the NYC quick-start fleet runs ~1,823 MW out of ~3,500 MW committed/available -- ~1,700 MW of genuine online headroom against a 500 MW NYC 10-min requirement (and a 250 MW spin sub-requirement). The reserve family therefore CANNOT bind: with the measured requirement and the modelled fleet the model says NYC is NOT synchronised-reserve-short, so no RCPF step fires and the NYC LMP does not separate upward. Commitment-gating only REMOVES offline (decommitted) pmax from the pool; it does nothing to the committed-but-backed-off headroom that actually dominates the NYC pocket, and reserve_adequacy_commit can only ADD committed headroom (it never tightens the pool). So the path-B premise -- that commitment would shrink the online pool below the requirement in tight hours -- is empirically false for NYISO at the measured requirement. INTERPRETATION (rules #1/#11/#12): the gap between the model (NYC reserve-rich) and reality (NYC measured reserve adder > $0 in ~4,000 h/yr) is NOT a missing online-gate; it is that NYISO's real downstate scarcity is driven by binding outside the static published reserve MW the model holds (effective real-time requirements that rise with conditions, deliverability/ramp limits inside the pocket, or unit energy commitments that consume the headroom the perfect-foresight LP keeps free). Manufacturing the tail by raising the requirement above the published value, steepening the RCPF, or adding a price adder is forbidden (rule #12). Both path A (online proxy, nyiso-29) and path B (commitment-gated, this run) are therefore confirmed insufficient with the grounded inputs; the downstate >$300 tail is left as an ACCEPTED, ledgered open frontier on the nyiso-27 keeper, NOT closed with an ungrounded knob. The path-B wiring stays a NYISO-only, default-OFF scaffold (byte-identical when off; 103 reserve/dispatch/commitment tests green); the full implementation is preserved in this bundle's model_changes.diff.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (NYC-peaker reserve/scarcity tail, incidence-gated; path B does not move it)
exceptions.reason: CT_PEAKER under-runs because NYC peakers clear on reserve/scarcity, not energy. Path B (commitment-gated synchronised reserve) does NOT move it: the NYC online headroom (~1,700 MW in tight hours) far exceeds the 250 MW spin / 500 MW 10-min requirement, so the reserve family never binds, no scarcity price forms, and the peakers stay economically idle exactly as in the keeper. Closing this needs a GROUNDED driver of real downstate scarcity that the static published reserve MW does not capture -- not an inflated requirement or a price adder (rule #12). Keeper stays nyiso-27.
